title: RFT, DPO, SFT: Fine-tuning with OpenAI — Ilan Bigio, OpenAI
talk_summary: OpenAI's Ilan Bigio explains SFT (imitation), DPO (preference deltas), and RFT (reward-graded reasoning) with demos on intent classification, joke generation, and email labeling. The core practical message is: don't fine-tune until prompting+evals plateau, and the real leverage is data quality and unambiguous graders, not the training algorithm.

takeaways.what_they_do: They run a parallel eval harness over a held-out set before and after any change, and only consider fine-tuning when prompt iteration stops improving the eval score.
takeaways.evidence_quote: always start with prompt engineering and see how far you can go and then run evals
takeaways.numbers: baseline 75% (4o-mini) / 83% (4o); fine-tuned models beat 03 and 4o on the task

takeaways.technique: Distill a big model into a small fast one for constrained tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Generate synthetic input/output pairs (deterministic permutation of schemas + GPT-4-generated natural inputs), filter, then SFT a small model to match the big model's accuracy at much lower latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we achieved GPT4 level performance at 3.5 accuracy
takeaways.numbers: within 2% of GPT-4 at a fraction of latency; 100 functions, low-to-mid thousands of examples

takeaways.technique: LLM-judge as reward/grader, built from existing evals
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues that if you already have a good LLM judge for evals, that same judge is the natural grader for RFT; the grader defines 'good' and the model maximizes it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start off build a good LM judge that captures the task you want to do well on and then you know try milk a model

takeaways.technique: Automated prompt tuning via failure-insight loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a forward pass on a minibatch, feed successes+failures to a reasoning model to extract 'notes' about what it got wrong, append notes to the prompt, re-eval on a held-out split, repeat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: let it reason over the failures and then maybe produce these insights
takeaways.numbers: demo did not improve (numbers 'not significantly' moving) — honest failure

takeaways.technique: Keep schemas in context; don't strip them for fine-tuning
takeaways.what_they_do: Tried removing function schemas/params from context to save tokens and found the model could not learn them well through fine-tuning; keeping them in context was necessary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: removing them from context makes them much harder to learn through fine-tuning

takeaways.technique: Data quality/noise dominates; small high-signal sets
takeaways.what_they_do: Shows RFT needs unambiguous, low-noise, high-signal data (40-80 examples can work) and that noisy/subjective labels (his email task) produce near-random results; SFT needs ~100-500 diverse examples and regresses on anything not covered.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's extremely sensitive to noisy data
takeaways.numbers: RFT: 40-80 high-signal examples; SFT: 100 to start, 500+ best; email RFT ~58% (near random)
